intro_html: Keeps a history book for the records you choose to watch: who created, changed, deleted, exported or opened each one, and what every changed value was before and after — so "who changed this supplier's bank account, and when?" becomes a question you can answer.

features.title: Watch Only What Matters
features.desc: Pick one kind of record at a time and tick exactly which of the five actions get recorded. Nothing is recorded until you switch a rule on.

features.title: Before and After, Side by Side
features.desc: Every change stores the old value next to the new one, on one screen you can search across every watched record at once.

features.title: A Copy of What Was Deleted
features.desc: Optionally keep the full contents of a record as it stood the moment it was deleted, so a removed record is still answerable.

features.title: See What Left the Building
features.desc: Spreadsheet exports are recorded too, with a button that reopens exactly the records that were exported.

features.title: One Person's Visit, Start to Finish
features.desc: Events are grouped into working sessions and the screen they came from, turning scattered entries into one readable story.

features.title: The Cost Is on the Screen
features.desc: Switching on view recording warns you first, in plain words: opening a list of 80 records records 80 events.

features.title: Clean-up You Turn On Yourself
features.desc: Retention is off by default — nothing deletes audit evidence unless you say so. Switched on, it works in batches and clears empty sessions too.

features.title: Two Roles, Both Checked
features.desc: An Auditor who reads but cannot change, and an Administrator who configures rules — each verified by signing in as that role, not as the account owner.

limitations: No tamper-proofing — an Audit Administrator can delete recorded history. This is an activity record, not a sealed evidence vault.
It only records. It never blocks, approves or reverses an action, and it never sends an alert.
No dashboards or charts — list, group and search only.
You can exclude people from recording, but you cannot restrict watching to a named set of people.
If recording itself fails, the user's own action still goes through — the failure goes to the server log rather than stopping their work.
View recording is skipped on read-only database replicas, so deployments that route reads to a replica will not record those views.
